answer: Neighborhood centrality weighting. Each agent’s influence is capped by the number of distinct, mutually non-adjacent neighborhoods it reaches, so a cluster of copies around one summit of connectivity counts as a single voice. Enforcement compares the local graph’s clustering to a global baseline, and identities sharing too many second-hop neighbors get their weight collapsed toward a haven of low reach. To fake breadth, an attacker must rent diverse links near a distant dune of the topology, paying real graph-distance costs per identity rather than cheap duplication.
